Elden Ring released and won a ton of game of the year awards all the way back in 2022, but the game isn’t going into retirement yet. Things have been quiet for most of this year, but a massive new update is releasing on August 28 for the FromSoftware open-world Soulslike.

The first big chunk of updates all related to laying the groundwork for the Tarnished Pack DLC, which releases on Friday, August 28, 2026. The following elements will be added upon purchase of the “Tarnished Pack” DLC.

Be sure to check back soon for lots more Elden Ring news and updates.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Switch 2 Review: 91 Score [2026]
items.summary: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition scores 91 on Metacritic at Switch 2 launch. 1080p/30fps, no DLSS, no cross-play — full review roundup and analysis.
items.content:
Sofia Lindström August 27, 2026 12 min read Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition went live on Nintendo Switch 2 on August 28, 2026, and the early critic verdict landed in a place few expected after months of rocky preview footage: strong. Metacritic has the port at 91 based on 40 critic reviews as of this morning, and OpenCritic’s tally sits at 88 with a 100% recommended rate. For a 220GB open-world action RPG built for PS5 and high-end PC squeezing onto a handheld hybrid, that’s the outcome Bandai Namco and FromSoftware needed after a demo build that reportedly ran as low as 15fps drew enough backlash that journalists were blocked from recording it, according to Tech Times .

What’s actually in the Tarnished Edition The technical numbers: 1080p and 30fps, no DLSS From 15fps demo disaster to a 91 Metacritic score What the reviews actually say Review scores at a glance How it stacks up against PS5, Xbox, and PC Why this port matters for Switch 2’s third-party lineup Historical context: FromSoftware and Nintendo hardware What outlets got wrong before release Predictions: where this goes from here Pricing and availability recap Frequently asked questions Related Coverage The $79.99 package bundles the base game, the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, and a new Tarnished Pack that adds weapons and Torrent armor cosmetics, according to IGN . It’s the first time Elden Ring has run on Nintendo hardware, and it arrives as one of the most technically demanding third-party ports Switch 2 has hosted to date. This is a news analysis of what shipped, how it runs, what critics said, and what the reception means for the platform’s third-party pipeline heading into the fall.

The Switch 2 SKU is a single package: the 2022 base game, the 2024 Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, and the new Tarnished Pack. IGN reported that the same additional content is being sold separately as paid DLC on PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X|S, and PC, meaning existing owners on other platforms don’t need to rebuy the whole game to get the new cosmetics and weapons. On Switch 2 it’s a single $79.99 purchase, and the physical release ships as an 80GB Game-Key Card rather than a card holding the full install, according to gagadget — meaning even boxed buyers download the bulk of the game.

Physical pre-orders opened June 5, 2026, with digital pre-orders following on June 11, per Tech Times’ reporting. Forbes contributor Brian Mazique confirmed the $79.99 U.S. price (£64.99 in the UK) and noted the release wasn’t published in a joint statement by Bandai Namco, FromSoftware, or Nintendo together — each handled its own announcement and regional pricing separately, a detail that matters for a AAA launch of this size.

There’s no Switch 2-exclusive quest content or new areas. The Tarnished Pack is cosmetic and equipment-focused: new weapons and the ability to reskin Torrent, the player’s spectral horse, with armor variants. Kotaku’s review was blunt about this, stating the edition “does not have any meaningful new features” — the pitch here is entirely about the port, not new Elden Ring content.

GamingBolt’s technical breakdown, published alongside the review embargo lift, is the most specific performance data available: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition runs at 1080p in both handheld and docked mode on Switch 2, and targets a 30fps cap in both modes rather than the 60fps some marketing materials and third-party wiki pages had floated earlier in the summer. GamingBolt also states the port is not using DLSS , which is notable given Switch 2’s custom Nvidia chip supports the tech and several other Switch 2 ports have leaned on it for frame generation and upscaling.

That’s a meaningful downgrade from the higher-resolution, higher-framerate modes available on PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC, where Elden Ring has offered both a resolution-priority mode and a 60fps performance mode since a 2022 patch. TechRadar’s review called the port “near-perfect” while flagging “minimal pop-in and occasionally stuttery enemy animations,” adding that performance is “otherwise so slick in handheld mode” that portability outweighs the technical compromises. Russian outlet iXBT, reviewing a late preview build in mid-August, reported the game “maintains around 30fps” in docked mode with “almost no noticeable stutters even during large-scale boss battles,” but described handheld mode as “somewhat more complex” — a softer framerate floor than docked play.

The gap between marketing claims and shipped performance is worth flagging on its own. A third-party guide site had published a claim, attributed to “the official Bandai Namco page,” that the Switch 2 version was “tuned for 60fps… in both docked and handheld modes.” That claim does not match what GamingBolt, iXBT, or TechRadar found in the actual shipped build, and no first-party Bandai Namco or FromSoftware statement reviewed for this piece confirms a 60fps target. Treat any 60fps claim for this specific SKU as unconfirmed pending a formal Digital Foundry-style technical teardown.

The story of this port didn’t start well. Tech Times’ headline framed it directly: “From 15fps Disaster to 30fps Delivery.” The outlet’s reporting says an early hands-on demo build ran badly enough — reportedly dipping to roughly 15fps in places — that Bandai Namco restricted journalists from recording footage of it, a move that historically signals a publisher trying to control damage from a build it already knows isn’t ready. That closed-door handling fed months of skepticism among Switch 2 owners and Souls fans, amplified by leaked or low-quality capture that circulated anyway.

CBR’s coverage of a later gameplay reveal, published in mid-August, captured the split reaction directly in its headline: “New Elden Ring Switch 2 Footage Doesn’t Put Fears To Rest.” CBR reported that even docked mode appeared to target 30fps rather than a higher ceiling, and that handheld footage “seems to dip below 30 FPS” in places — suggesting the optimization pass was still incomplete just two weeks before launch. RPG Site’s preview, filed after hands-on time with a build closer to final, struck a more optimistic tone: “in handheld mode, the game now appears to be a solid 30FPS, and with a resolution either hitting or very visibly close to a native 1080p,” adding that even once in-game rain effects kicked in, “the game hit the 30FPS target consistently.”

items.title: Call of Duty, Elden Ring, Bluey, and More Titles Bring Big Week to Gaming
items.summary: Switch 2 releases, family-friendly adventures, and financial literacy games arriving in the gaming world.
items.content:
Nintendo is sharing a major dose of new content this week, while updates and announcements across the broader gaming landscape bring new ways to play, create, learn, and compete. From Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and Elden Ring Tarnished Edition to CookieRun: Crumble , new active games from Nex, and a new title from Bluey, the latest slate spans blockbuster franchises, family-focused experiences, educational titles, and competitive gaming.

Nintendo Switch 2 players have plenty to dig into this week, with the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Open Beta serving as the biggest addition. Running Aug. 28-Sept. 1, Open Beta gives all Switch 2 players access to a playable Campaign mission, multiplayer modes and in-game rewards. Players can also use the Vault Edition operators and weapons during the beta, even without a preorder. The full game launches Oct. 23, with preorders available in Nintendo eShop. Meanwhile, Orbitals , a two-player co-op adventure set in a retro anime-inspired universe, launches Sept. 3.

Two major titles also arrive on Switch 2 this week. Elden Ring Tarnished Edition launches Aug. 28, bringing the base game, Shadow Of the Erdtree expansion, new weapons and armor, and additional customization options to Nintendo’s latest console. Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 is also now available on both Switch 2 and Switch , featuring Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriot s and Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker .

Beyond the major releases, Nintendo eShop adds a wide range of new games across Switch 2 and Switch, including Another Crab’s Treasure — Nintendo Switch 2 Edition , Lou’s Lagoon , Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault , Dogpile , Golftacular! , Magnetail , and Tearscape . Several additional titles are scheduled to launch over the coming days, including My Friendly Little Island Deluxe Aug. 29, Forest of Deceit Aug. 31, and Lamp Clicker and Metal Garden Sept. 1.

Nintendo Music is also expanding this week with a SimCity playlist featuring tracks from the Super NES classic game, along with additional Mario Kart World content and bonus tracks. My Nintendo is offering a chance to win a Limited Edition Deluxe The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild Vinyl Soundtrack Boxset, while new rewards include a Pokémon Pokopia notebook and Star Fox collectible patch set.

Finally, Nintendo’s Blockbuster Sale kicks off with deals on digital games for Nintendo Switch 2 and Nintendo Switch. The sale runs through Sept. 9, giving players another opportunity to pick up games at a discount alongside this week’s new releases.

CookieRun: Crumble is expanding its gameplay lineup with its first major update since launching globally four weeks ago. The new update introduces Guild Conquest, a cooperative raid mode that lets guildmates work together to take on bosses, along with cross-server guild competition, new rewards, and three playable Cookies: Brightseeker Cookie, Pinot Noir Cookie, and Guild Medal-exclusive Tea Knight Cookie. The deck-building auto-battler has surpassed 2.5 million players and KRW 20 billion ($14.3 million) in revenue since launch, with the U.S. ranking as its top-grossing market outside Korea. Meanwhile, CookieRun: Kingdom also received an update on Aug. 26, adding Episode 9 of Timeline of Fate, “Unofficial Futures,” plus Super Epic Time Shadow Cookie, Epic Pulpo Cookie, and a new Legendary costume for Silent Salt Cookie.

Bluey’s Happy Snaps is heading to major gaming platforms this October, inviting families to explore familiar locations from the hit series, snap photos, collect stickers, and build their own Bluey scrapbook. The adventure features two-player co-op as Bluey and Bingo, along with activities designed to encourage creativity, exploration, and play beyond the screen.

The game will be available digitally and physically, with special editions offering additional holiday gifting options, including an Amazon-exclusive Deluxe Edition and a Target-exclusive Activity Book Edition .

Coolmath Games has launched CountForward by Coolmath Games , a new suite of free financial literacy games designed to teach students about earning, saving, spending, investing, and protecting money. The six- game collection has already generated more than 3 million plays in beta and was developed with educational experts to align with state financial literacy curricula and national standards.

The platform is also launching a teacher pilot program to bring the games into classrooms and gather educator feedback, with more titles planned for the school year. The initial lineup includes games focused on investing, taxes, budgeting, saving, and financial decision-making, including a multiplayer trivia game that supports up to 50 players.

Finch partners with DreamWorks Animation’s Forgotten Island ahead of the film’s Sept. 25 release with a limited-time in-app event launching Sept. 1.

The month-long experience features a 14-day story adventure inspired by Filipino folklore, along with a new Duwende-inspired micropet, island-themed outfits, décor, and exclusive colorways. The app, and event, encourage users to build daily self-care habits centered on friendship, gratitude, reflection, and connection.

Nex is expanding its active family gaming platform into new international markets while adding two iconic franchises to the Nex Playground lineup. The company plans to bring Nex Playground to Germany later this year, followed by a broader European and Asian expansion in 2027, while Sonic Forces: Rival Rush and PAC-MAN are set to join the platform this fall.

items.title: Patch Notes Version 1.17
items.summary: Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING . This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC , scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026 , and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before
items.content:
Patch 1.17 has been released for ELDEN RING. This patch aims to bring support the Tarnished Pack DLC, scheduled for release on Friday, August 28, 2026, and to implement gameplay balance adjustments. Please apply the latest update before playing.

MAIN UPDATE ADDITIONS

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

The following elements will be added upon purchase of the "Tarnished Pack" DLC.
  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.
  • Added weapons that can be purchased from merchants or found in the Lands Between.
  • Added three types of Spectral Steed Attire that change the appearance of Torrent: - Tree Sentinel Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Stormveil Castle. - Silver of Caria Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Liurnia of the Lakes. - Funereal Night Spectral Steed Attire: Found in Altus Plateau. Note: After obtaining any Spectral Steed Attire, the option to change the spectral steed’s appearance will be added to the Site of Grace menu.
  • Added an NPC invasion event in Caelid.
  • Added an NPC invasion event in Leyndell, Royal Capital. Note: This event will not occur after the area has changed to Leyndell, Ashen Capital.
The "Tarnished Pack" release times are as follows: Steam: Friday, August 28 at 7:00 JST | 00:00 CEST | 15:00 PDT.

Balance Adjustments

Changed certain items found in the field or obtained by defeating certain powerful enemies in the Realm of Shadow to higher-tier items or other treasures. Note: Items already that were already found will not be changed.

Weapons

  • Smithscript Dagger / Rellana's Twin Blades → Increased critical hit power.
  • Smithscript Axe / Smithscript Spear / Spear of the Impaler → Reduced the stamina consumption of weapon-throwing attacks. → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.
  • Carian Sorcery Sword → Changed Intelligence scaling so that it now increases the attack power of all damage types.
  • Smithscript Greathammer → Increased the power of weapon-throwing attacks.
  • Golem Fist → Increased the range of the fist-launching heavy attack.
  • Firespark Perfume Bottle / Lightning Perfume Bottle / Chilling Perfume Bottle / Frenzyflame Perfume Bottle / Deadly Poison Perfume Bottle → Increased attack power.
  • Lordsworn's Shield / Briar Greatshield / Spiked Palisade Shield / Icon Shield / Golden Beast Crest Shield / Manor Towershield / Crossed-Tree Towershield / Inverted Hawk Towershield / Dragon Towershield / Distinguished Greatshield / Gilded Greatshield / Black Steel Greatshield / Ant's Skull Plate / Erdtree Greatshield → Increased guard boost. → Reduced weight.
  • Wooden Greatshield / Cuckoo Greatshield / Redmane Greatshield / Golden Greatshield / Crucible Hornshield / Dragonclaw Shield / Eclipse Crest Greatshield / Jellyfish Shield / One-Eyed Shield → Increased guard boost.
  • Haligtree Crest Greatshield → Reduced weight.
  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased the time before an attack can be performed with a right-hand weapon immediately after attacking with this weapon equipped in the left hand.

Skills

  • Parry → Improved parry performance. → Reduced the time before various actions can be performed after activation when used with Daggers, Curved Swords, or Small Shields.
  • Storm Wall → Changed the skill so that it no longer consumes FP when used. → Improved parry performance.
  • Thops's Barrier → Improved parry performance.

Sorceries

  • Founding Rain of Stars → Increased power.
  • Carian Retaliation → Increased power.
  • Meteorite → Reduced casting time.
  • Meteorite of Astel → Reduced casting time.
  • Gravitational Missile → Changed the spell so that the gravity projectile does not explode immediately upon striking terrain such as the ground or a wall.

Incantations

  • Feather of the Divine Bird → Increased power.
  • O, Flame! → Expanded attack range.
  • Rain of Fire → Increased power.

PvP-Exclusive Balance Adjustments

Weapons

  • Rakshasa's Great Katana → Increased damage taken from attacks by other players while attacking.

Incantations

  • Rugalea's Roar → Reduced power against other players.
  • Rotten Breath / Ekzykes's Decay → Reduced the amount of time other player characters are unable to move from hit reactions when struck by these incantations.

Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug where critical hits dealt with Great Katana weapon types had lower-than-expected power against large enemies. Fixed a bug where jumping attacks with Great Katana weapon types could be parried.

PC-Only Bug Fixes

Fixed a bug that prevented camera control with the mouse during NPC dialogue when using keyboard and mouse controls Fixed a bug in the "Keyboard/Mouse Settings" section of the system menu in which selecting the reset option did not restore various settings to their defaults The version number shown in the lower-right corner of the title screen after applying this update will be as follows:

App Ver. 1.17 Regulation Ver. 1.17

This update is required for online play.

We will continue to make improvements so that you can enjoy ELDEN RING more comfortably. Thank you for your continued support.

items.title: Review: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition (Nintendo Switch 2)
items.content:
Elden Ring is an incredible game, and I already have a very in-depth review covering why I consider it to be a genuine masterpiece within the “games-as-art” canon. I’m not going to re-litigate that in reviewing the Switch 2 release of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition. Everything that applied to that original review applies here as well. In fact, it’s genuinely impressive just how completely the gothic ambience translates to the Switch’s relatively humble screen.

Just to be up-front about this though: the Switch 2 version of Elden Ring is a slight downgrade from its big console and PC brothers. It’s truly impressive that the downgrade manifests itself in such minor ways, with loading times that are a second or two longer, or a framerate that is very steady, but not quite as silken. However, those compromises (particularly the frame rate) do matter for a game that is as demanding on timing and precision as Elden Ring is.

There’s also a small issue from the hardware itself. The Switch 2’s Joy-Cons don’t offer quite the same nuanced travel as a standard controller, so if you’re playing the game in handheld mode, you’ve got ever-so-slightly less depth of control. Again, it by no means makes Elden Ring unplayable, but, again, for a game as demanding on its players as Elden Ring, those tiny nuances will matter. The long and short of it is that if you’re playing Elden Ring on another platform, I’m not 100% sure you’ll be sold on grabbing it on Switch 2 as well. I, personally, much prefer the portability and am happy for the compromises for that form factor, but I also realise that I’m something of an outlier in that regard.

Mind you, none of what I said didn’t apply to the Nintendo Switch port of Dark Souls back in the day, and when I log into that game from time to time I still see the occasional ghostly outline wandering around. Clearly there is an audience for these things, and I don’t want to understate just how impressive it is that an open world as drenched in atmosphere and expansive in scope as Elden Ring is plays on the Switch 2. And you get the universally celebrated expansion, Shadow of the Erdtree, to go with the universally celebrated base game. The world looks utterly gorgeous on the Switch 2’s screen, and while I was initially concerned that the smaller form factor would make it harder to make out key details, I’ve had no issue whatsoever in making my way around the world again.

The only other downside that needs to be noted is the multiplayer. Perhaps because the frame rates between versions are slightly different (which would make things much tougher for a Switch 2 player), Elden Ring’s multiplayer isn’t cross-play. You can only team up with or go to war with other Switch 2 players. This is a bummer to people who might have wanted to buddy up with specific players on a different platform, but, again, I do have to note that Dark Souls had no issue with the multiplayer experience being populated on the Switch, and I cannot imagine that the long-term case will be any different for Elden Ring. This is one of those games that most people would feel an urge to own, so if you’re counting on getting some randoms into your game to help with one of the bosses, I would be surprised if you’re waiting for long.

This has been a difficult review to write. Firstly, because everything that makes Elden Ring a special experience is not exclusive to the Switch 2 release, I really recommend you read my review of the original game to get an understanding of just how strongly I feel about this game. Everything I wrote in that review applies here too. But also, in acknowledging that the Switch 2 port of Elden Ring isn’t quite up to the standard of the game playing on the PlayStation 5, this review sounds more negative than it should. The differences are a rounding error, and what is important is that this masterpiece runs perfectly well on a very portable console.

items.title: How to utterly embarrass yourself while "playing" Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2
items.summary: Look: although I have the privilege of writing about video games for this fine outlet, this does not, by any measure, mean I am always good at said video games. Everyone here on the Nintendo Everything team has a genre or two they know like the back of their hand, and I can tell you with complete certainty that Soulslike...
items.content:
Look: although I have the privilege of writing about video games for this fine outlet, this does not, by any measure, mean I am always good at said video games. Everyone here on the Nintendo Everything team has a genre or two they know like the back of their hand, and I can tell you with complete certainty that Soulslike games are not my area of expertise. Regardless, the Nintendo Switch 2 port of Elden Ring and its Shadow of the Erdtree expansion – now bundled as the Tarnished Edition – remains one of the biggest third-party releases on the console this year, and I figured this would be a great opportunity to see if I was cut out for the challenge of one of 2022’s top-rated games.

Spoilers: I was not cut out for said challenge.

If you want to learn all about how to make an absolute fool of yourself while playing Elden Ring on Nintendo Switch 2, read on.

Elden Ring has a remarkably robust character creator that lets you adjust practically every pore of your warrior’s face. I can’t recall the last time I played a game in which I had so many distinct ways to negligibly adjust the size and positioning of a character’s nose and nostrils. And of course, all of this is a critical step towards getting immersed in the adventure to come.

I probably should have spent the same amount of time considering my character’s class. I opted to go into this game completely blind, so I just flipped through the list of classes and picked the one that seemed the most relevant to how I would normally play an action RPG, ultimately landing on the Bandit class. This seemed to be wise at the outset, because I figured that having a bow as well as a blade would be useful, probably leaving me well-equipped for most foes I would encounter in the early game.

While it wasn’t a horrible choice, I did find myself wishing pretty quickly that I had opted for a build with some more oomph. Having a knife that I could swing quickly felt good, as it allowed me to be nimble, but at least in the early game I didn’t get a ton of use out of having a bow on hand. Meanwhile, the character I made – a snow-haired stud I named Alabaster – spent 80% of his screen time with his face obscured by armor. Go figure. The good news is that, as the game progresses, there are plenty of ways to customize both your playstyle and your look, so you’re not locked into anything major.

How this version of Elden Ring might perform has been the subject of much conversation prior to launch. A world as sprawling and moody as The Lands Between is typically something I’d want to experience on the biggest screen possible. So it’s a real shame that I spent as much time fighting the game’s frame rate as I did fighting Godrick Knights – in docked mode, at least.

It’s not unplayable by any means, but it’s also far from perfect. Elden Ring’s docked frame rate heavily fluctuates depending on what is happening onscreen; generally it seemed like the more interesting the environment was, the more often I would encounter issues. There were times when it was so noticeable that it even made Alabaster’s running animation look a bit stilted. The game itself looks really good on the big screen – although not quite comparable to other platforms in terms of fine details – but given the scale of the world, the density of foliage and foes, and the very impressive lighting effects, it’s an understandable compromise.

In handheld mode, though, the game looks and runs immaculately. It’s a bewildering experience playing a game like this on such a slim device, and the fact that it looks as crisp and runs as smooth as it does in this mode is truly a miracle. I would also say that the smaller screen helps mask some of the DLSS and (what appears to be) dynamic resolution scaling better than while playing in docked mode.

I mean, sure, that giant tentacle monster slithering along the beach doesn’t look like a friendly fella, but it’s in the game’s opening section of the map. The developers wouldn’t seriously place such a high level foe right in the way of a player who is just trying to wander of the beaten path only a little, would they?

I know I shouldn’t be too surprised that Elden Ring doesn’t hesitate to destroy players who get a little too big for their britches, but it’s not just the big beasts that will KO you. Just about anything in this game can pose a serious threat if you are underleveled, underequipped, or underskilled as a player. I definitely felt like I fit into all three of those categories… well, the entire time I spent playing Elden Ring, really.

This game, in fact, does have quite a few similarities to Nintendo’s highly acclaimed Zelda adventure. Extremely sparse storytelling that’s mostly delivered as a by-product of exploration? Check. A cool horse? Check. Picking up resources to craft stuff and cook? Check. A wide open world that is so unfathomably massive that you wonder if you will ever possibly see everything in it? Check.

So, you’ll have to forgive my muscle memory as I repeatedly tried to climb things that could not be climbed (read: most things), jump over things that could not be jumped over, and casually wander into places that, apparently, are always filled with dangerous creatures that can wreck me in about 2 hits. In the opening area? And people play these games… for fun?!

Very early on in Elden Ring, I stumbled across a little camp of soldiers across from a huge castle gate. With my (theoretically) lighter and stealthier build, I figured I could probably just off them one by one without raising the alarm. I also figured there was probably some good stuff tucked away in there that would help me not be so much of a pushover.

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition review – A great port of a phenomenal game
Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Switch 2 means you can now touch grace AND grass
Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Review – A New Way To Experience A Classic
items.summary: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is excellent on the Nintendo Switch 2, but a few issues remain.
items.content:
Elden Ring has entranced minds, frustrated gamers, and created a sense of wonder since 2022. If you’ve never played Elden Ring, whether that’s because you were never interested or because you only owned a Switch, today’s your lucky day! Fellow Tarnished, your Switch 2 is ready for its first site of grace. Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition gives us two new character bases and my personal favorite, a chance to start the journey all over again. Game Name: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition Platform(s): Xbox Series X/S, PS5, PC, and Nintendo Switch 2 Reviewed on: Nintendo Switch 2 Developer: FromSoftware Publisher: Bandai Namco Release Date: August 28th, 2026 I am so happy to see that Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree are coming to the Switch 2. A new audience will fall to the whims of gravity, fighting an endgame boss at level one, and making their way to becoming Elden Lord. If you were dancing with the idea of getting a Switch 2, I would say that now is the time to buy. With how many titles are getting either a bump up in FPS, a remaster, or making their Switch 2 debut, it’s the perfect time to invest in this console.

Never in my wildest dreams did I think that Elden Ring would find its way to the Switch. I’m so excited for everyone whose only console is a Switch 2 to experience this game. Now, while I do have a bias for Elden Ring and Shadow of the Erdtree (platinumed it twice, the first time on Xbox, the second time on Steam), there are still some things left to be desired with this port. Firstly, the lighting is incredibly dark in certain parts. When it comes to games and the ambiance they create, I’m a huge proponent of leaving the world as it was designed unless it needs to be changed by the player for accessibility reasons.

I would highly recommend ramping up the lighting in settings, then adjusting image quality and changing it to your preferred setting from there. When I first started in Castleward Tunnel, it was incredibly dark; I couldn’t see much besides the site of grace, identifiers like the way to the boss, and the way I came into the tunnel. When I changed the settings, I felt the change was only incremental, and not substantially helpful. I could see a bit more, but it was still dark. Another thing that I thought would have been fixed this time around, is the ability to enhance the font-size in Elden Ring and its DLC. Launching on a new console has its trials and tribulations, but with how big FromSoftware is, I would have expected them to amp up the accessibility features this time around. If you can add two new classes, you can add accessibility that helps players maneuver throughout the beautiful world you’ve built. I’ve always been a critic of FromSoftware’s accessibility in Elden Ring. I guess I should just put these foolish ambitions to rest.

So why now, why get Elden Ring now? Having been available for four years on Xbox, PS5, and PC, why release this game on a new system now and not when it first launched? Now I don’t have interviews in my back pocket to pull out for this review to give you a definitive answer, but I do have an educated guess as to why. Firstly, reaching a wider audience is key. FromSoftware probably saw a gap in the market that wasn’t being filled by Elden Ring and wanted to fix that. Also, exclusives are a big move in the FromSoftware playbook; that’s not to say that’s a negative thing, it just is what it is.

In the Switch 2 version of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition, there are two new classes available, Idus Knight and Heavy Knight. Much like the console exclusivity of Bloodborne or Demon’s Souls to the PlayStation, having classes locked behind a Switch 2 copy of Elden Ring will be reason enough for people to buy it. The two new classes, by the way, are incredibly fun to play around with. Just imagine a bleed build with the Idus Knight? Do I think the exclusivity of two classes is a bit much, yes, but I also think It might be there as an incentive to buy Elden Ring on the Switch 2. Amongst a plethora of things, come over to the dark side, we have NPC’s with main character syndrome, and an entrancing world to get lost in.

As for my experience and how the game flowed on the Switch 2, I didn’t find any major issues. Other than what I’ve mentioned, it was like I was playing Elden Ring on the PC or console post-patches. No, not the annoying, kick you down a hole Patches. Margit the Fell Omen was just as mad as ever that I was there, and Melina created a cozy spot near a site of grace for me to sit. I would catch myself getting lost in the world, looking back at the clock, and two hours had passed.

Playing this game was incredibly smooth with stable performance. I was crossing my fingers that everything would work the way it’s supposed to, and I’m so happy that it did. Moving through the world, I was trying to do several things at once to “break the game” so to speak. Like riding Torrent while fighting enemies that you find out in the world, or randomly falling from great heights, just to see if the game would crash, and there was nothing. No crashes, blips, or even pop-ins. I think people who only own a Switch 2 or who own multiple consoles, plus a Switch 2, will love the port of this game. While, of course, there are no achievements, it’s nice to roam the world, explore, experiment with builds, and do things you might not want to do on your main build.

As someone who owns every console (plus a Steam Deck and PC), the only thing that gets tricky is remembering which buttons are which when going from playing PS5 to the Switch 2. Besides getting used to the button layout, this port is everything I could have hoped for. I really love the fact that the pop-ins are non-existent, which is rare for a lot of Switch games to not have on release, or before the first wave of patches come out.

I took a look at how the game performs across console, PC, Steam Deck, and now the Switch 2. I’d like to focus in for a moment comparing the game’s performance on the Switch 2 versus the PC. Since the PC is what I have the most hours in, sitting at 120 hours, I feel like it’s the fairest piece of tech to use as a comparison. When the PC version of Elden Ring launched, it was a mess; now, keep in mind, I didn’t get the PC version until a year later. While several patches came out, and efforts were taken to make the best possible version it could be, it was still a hot mess.

Playing Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition on the Switch 2 feels like FromSoftware learned from the PC release and shipped a smooth, day-one version with no performance issues. Other than the issues I mention in this review, which I feel are more quality-of-life fixes than a day-one patch. The Switch 2 version, by far, runs smoother than the PC version when it launched. While the PC version of Elden Ring runs really well, there will still be minor performance issues from time to time. With the Switch 2 version, I feel that this might be the best the game has been optimized. Who knows, I might find some issues later on, but as of now, the performance of Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition is incredible!

I greatly enjoyed my time so far with the Switch 2 port of Elden Ring! While the image quality/brightness suffers a bit in handheld mode, I saw no visible bugs, issues, pop-ins, or anything that hindered the gameplay experience. If you’ve been wanting to check out Elden Ring and its DLC, but had no way to play until now, I would highly recommend investing in Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition!

Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition will release August 28th, 2026, for Nintendo Switch 2

Review Disclosure Statement : Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition was provided to us by Bandai Namco. For more information on how we review video games and other media/technology, please review our Review Guideline/Scoring Policy .

With two new classes exclusive to the Switch 2, FromSoftware brings the best day-one performance of Elden Ring I’ve ever seen. While the image quality, brightness, and ability to change the font size were lacking, this port runs incredibly well!

items.content:
Who among us doesn't love to sever the Dreadnodus?

(Image credit: Hoyoverse) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter As the opening reveal of this year's Gamescom Opening Night Live, HoYoverse brought its first official look at Nodusfall—a change of pace for the gacha game behemoth that looks a little bit Elden Ring , a lot bit Monster Hunter, and a whole pile of proper nouns added for good measure.

While I like to think it takes more to catch my attention than forcefully mashing together two things I think are neat, I'd be lying if I said I wasn't tempted by the idea. If there's one thing Monster Hunter monsters have been missing, it's FromSoft-style primordial depression.

Watch On From the looks of things, there's more than enough metaphysical malaise to go around in Nodusfall. The laws of divinity have apparently frayed, plunging creation into a state of cosmic disarray. There are 10 suns now. Ideally, there's only supposed to be one of those. Not great!

Luckily for those of us who like to be given an excuse to try to fight a lizard 30 times our size, all that profound devastation seems to have produced a wide selection of giant, charismatic creatures to swordfight alongside your friends. In the reveal trailer embedded above, I saw giant bears, some sort of giant pack foxes, a horned, winged manticore, and a dragon or two (giant). I don't yet know how Nodusfall's progression works, but if I'm not allowed to harvest all their individual pieces and turn them into pants, I'm going to feel personally betrayed.

While the glimpses of combat shown in the footage looks like it hews pretty closely to the pace and rhythm of Monster Hunter, Nodusfall does seem to be dropping a few original elements into the mix. At one point, one of the player characters uses some sort of transformation ability to become a giant, armored knight in the middle of a hunt. And later, two players perform an elaborate, paired execution animation.

HoYoverse's Nodusfall is free to play but isn't a typical gacha game: 'Characters are not obtained through random draws' Mistfall Hunter's demo might finally convince me, a souls sicko, to give extraction games a proper go—even if it's more modern God of War than Nightreign The next game in a huge Chinese action RPG series has plenty of action, but I hope it hasn't totally abandoned the RPG What remains to be seen is what sort of monetization scheme Nodusfall will be wrapped in—something that HoYoverse's history doesn't exactly inspire confidence about. If I have to do gacha pulls for a gunlance, I'm going to have a hard time.

Nodusfall doesn't have much of an online presence yet, so it'll likely be a while before we can expect a release date.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stoneveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.title: ELDEN RING: SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE – Official Vinyl Soundtrack
items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States

items.title: Discover the ELDEN RING Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp
items.summary: Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING ’s most iconic character. Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique n
items.content:
Summon the legendary warrior into your world with the Blaidd The Half-Wolf Lamp, a handcrafted, LED-powered tribute to one of ELDEN RING’s most iconic character.

Designed for collectors, lore enthusiasts, and Tarnished alike, this unique night lamp captures the tragic loyalty and silent strength of Blaidd, Shadow of Ranni.

The lamp features an LED-illuminated base that reveals glowing rune symbols beneath Blaidd’s feet, evoking the grace-given power that guides Tarnished across the Lands Between. Rising above it, an engraved acrylic summoning panel glows softly when lit, capturing the look and feel of an in-game summon sign and the spirit-calling magic it represents. Powered through a simple USB connection, it offers effortless illumination for any desk, gaming setup, or collector’s display.

"If ever thou shouldst call upon me… I shall come."

Blaidd’s oath echoes still. Now, he stands ready, not for battle, but as a silent guardian of your space.

Bring the moonlit magic of ELDEN RING into your world, one glowing rune at a time.

*This edition is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia and the United States.
